이름.t: To elders, ask politely: 성함이 어떻게 되세요?

볼펜.x: Please write your name with a black pen.
볼펜.t: Koreans say 볼펜 for an ordinary pen; 펜 is also used.

반지.x: She's wearing a pretty ring on her left hand.
반지.t: Rings are worn with 끼다, not 입다: 반지를 끼다 "put on a ring"; take off is 빼다.

미술.x: I went to an art exhibition with a friend on the weekend.
미술.t: 미술 means visual art; 예술 is art in the broad sense, including music and dance.

와인.x: I drank wine with my friends at the birthday party.
와인.e: From English 'wine'; for alcohol in general, Koreans say 술.

아무.t: 아무도 needs a negative verb ('nobody'), while 아무나 means 'anyone at all' with positive verbs.

최근.x: I recently bought a new phone.
최근.t: Use 최근에 as an adverb ('recently') and 최근 + noun for 'recent ___'.

알람.x: I didn't hear the alarm, so I overslept.
알람.t: Set an alarm: 알람을 맞추다; turn it off: 알람을 끄다. Snoozing again and again is a very relatable morning struggle.

알레르기.ex: 저는 땅콩 알레르기가 있어서 조심해야 해요.
알레르기.x: I'm allergic to peanuts, so I have to be careful.
알레르기.e: From German 'Allergie,' not English 'allergy' — hence the 'reu-gi' ending.
알레르기.t: To say you're allergic, use 알레르기가 있다: 고양이 알레르기가 있어요.

교통 체증.ex: 출근 시간에는 교통 체증이 아주 심해요.
교통 체증.x: Traffic is really bad during the morning rush hour.
교통 체증.e: Literally 'traffic stuck-symptom'; 체증 on its own also means indigestion.
교통 체증.t: In conversation people usually say 차가 막혀요; 교통 체증 sounds like news or writing.

겨우.forms: 겨우 + verb (barely): 겨우 도착했어요; 겨우 + amount (only): 겨우 천 원
겨우.x: I woke up late and barely caught the bus.
겨우.t: Before a number, 겨우 means 'only, a mere': 겨우 다섯 명 'only five people'.

규칙적.x: I exercise regularly for my health.
규칙적.t: Use 규칙적인 before nouns (규칙적인 생활) and 규칙적으로 before verbs.

문자 메시지.ex: 집에 도착하면 문자 메시지를 보내 주세요.
문자 메시지.x: Please send me a text when you get home.
문자 메시지.t: People usually shorten it to 문자: 문자 보낼게요 means 'I'll text you.'

대문.ex: 집에 들어가기 전에 대문을 꼭 잠그세요.
대문.x: Be sure to lock the front gate when you go in.
대문.e: Literally 'big door' — the gate to a house's yard.

심리.ex: 사람의 심리를 이해하는 것은 쉽지 않아요.
심리.t: Pronounced [심니] — ㄹ after ㅁ becomes ㄴ.

인공지능.ex: 요즘은 인공지능으로 번역도 하고 그림도 그려요.
인공지능.x: These days people translate and even draw pictures with AI.
인공지능.t: In everyday speech people also just say AI (에이아이).

경쟁사.x: A competitor released a similar product first.

결제하다.m: to pay (for), to make a payment, to settle
결제하다.x: I'll pay for the meal by card.
결제하다.e: Literally 'decide and settle' — completing a transaction.
결제하다.t: Don't confuse with 결재하다 (to approve a document) — same pronunciation, different word.

보전.ex: 자연 보전을 위해 쓰레기를 줄여야 해요.
보전.x: We need to reduce trash to conserve nature.
보전.t: Often confused with 보존: 보전 keeps something healthy and intact, 보존 keeps it unchanged, like artifacts.

입이 가볍다.forms: 입이 가벼워요 · 입이 가벼웠어요 · 입이 가벼운 사람 (ㅂ irregular)
입이 가볍다.m: to be a blabbermouth, to be unable to keep a secret
입이 가볍다.x: That person can't keep a secret, so be careful.
입이 가볍다.e: Literally 'one's mouth is light' — it opens too easily.

단연.ex: 이 식당의 인기 메뉴는 단연 불고기예요.
단연.x: The most popular dish at this restaurant is by far the bulgogi.
단연.e: Literally 'cut-off so': decisive, with no room for doubt.
단연.t: Pronounced [다년]; pairs with 최고, 으뜸, or 1위 to mean 'the clear winner'.

차츰.forms: 차츰 + change verb: 차츰 나아지다, 차츰 익숙해지다
차츰.ex: 새 회사 생활에 차츰 익숙해지고 있어요.
차츰.x: I'm gradually getting used to life at my new company.

그뿐 아니라.forms: A. 그뿐 아니라 B; also: 그뿐만 아니라
그뿐 아니라.ex: 이 식당은 음식이 맛있어요. 그뿐 아니라 가격도 싸요.
그뿐 아니라.x: This restaurant has delicious food. Not only that, it's cheap too.
그뿐 아니라.t: The following clause usually takes 도: 그뿐 아니라 B도 ~.

이를테면.forms: 이를테면 + example: 이를테면 사과나 배 같은 과일
이를테면.m: for example, for instance, so to speak
이를테면.ex: 저는 단 음식, 이를테면 케이크나 초콜릿을 좋아해요.
이를테면.x: I like sweet foods, for example cake or chocolate.
이를테면.e: Contracted from 이를 터이면 'if I am to say it'; 이르다 means 'to say'.
이를테면.t: More conversational than 예컨대; in everyday speech 예를 들면 is the most common choice.

비유하다.m: to compare (figuratively), to liken, to use a metaphor
비유하다.ex: 사람들은 인생을 긴 여행에 비유하곤 해요.
비유하다.x: People often compare life to a long journey.
비유하다.e: Literally 'compare to illustrate' — explaining one thing through another.
비유하다.t: Pattern: A를 B에 비유하다 = to liken A to B.

꾸짖다.x: The teacher scolded the student who came late.
꾸짖다.t: 꾸짖다 sounds formal or literary; in everyday speech 혼내다 is more common.

수월하다.x: My friend helped, so the move went smoothly.
수월하다.t: Often in comparisons: 생각보다 수월했다 (easier than expected), 훨씬 수월해지다.

자취.m: living on your own (away from family, cooking for yourself)
자취.ex: 대학교 때부터 혼자 자취를 하고 있어요.
자취.x: I've been living on my own since college.
자취.t: Don't confuse with homonym 자취 'trace, track' (발자취 'footprints').

본선.ex: 한국은 월드컵 본선에 열 번 넘게 진출했어요.
본선.x: Korea has qualified for the World Cup finals more than ten times.
본선.e: Literally 'main selection' — the stage after the prelims.

불판.x: Could you change the grill plate, please?
불판.t: At Korean BBQ places staff replace a charred plate for free when you ask; 불판을 갈다 is the set phrase.

한과.x: I got a box of traditional Korean sweets as a Lunar New Year gift.
한과.e: Literally 'Korean confection'; a general name for traditional sweets such as 약과 and 유과.
한과.t: Most 한과 are fried, pressed or candied with honey or grain syrup rather than baked.

채무.ex: 회사는 채무를 갚기 위해 건물을 팔았어요.
채무.x: The company sold its building to pay off its debts.
채무.e: Literally 'debt duty' — the obligation to pay back.
채무.t: 채무자 is the debtor and 채권자 the creditor; in everyday talk people just say 빚.

관세.x: The government imposed tariffs on imported cars.
관세.e: Literally 'gate tax' — paid at the border checkpoint.

여론몰이.m: drumming up public opinion, opinion manipulation
여론몰이.ex: 일부 언론의 여론몰이에 대한 비판이 커지고 있습니다.
여론몰이.x: Criticism is growing over some media outlets' manipulation of public opinion.
여론몰이.e: 여론 'public opinion' + native 몰이 'herding, driving' — herding public opinion like animals.

선의.x: Something I said with good intentions was misunderstood.

경각심.ex: 이번 사고는 안전에 대한 경각심을 일깨웠습니다.
경각심.x: This accident raised awareness about safety.
경각심.t: Collocations: 경각심을 갖다 'stay alert' and 경각심을 일깨우다 'raise awareness'.

가문.ex: 그는 대대로 학자를 배출한 가문 출신이에요.
가문.x: He comes from a family that has produced scholars for generations.
가문.e: Literally 'house gate', meaning the household line.

견인하다.m: to tow; to drive, to lead (growth)
견인하다.ex: 반도체 수출이 경제 성장을 견인하고 있습니다.
견인하다.x: Semiconductor exports are driving economic growth.
견인하다.e: Literally 'pull and draw' — towing a car or pulling an economy forward.
견인하다.t: Signs saying 견인 지역 mean illegally parked cars will be towed.

추스르다.forms: 추슬러요 · 추슬렀어요 · 추스를 거예요 · 추스르세요 (르 irregular)
추스르다.m: to pull (oneself) together, to recover; to hitch up (clothes, a load)
추스르다.ex: 그는 큰 충격을 받았지만 곧 마음을 추슬렀어요.
추스르다.x: He was badly shaken but soon pulled himself together.
추스르다.t: Often 몸을 추스르다 'to recover physically' or 마음을 추스르다 'to recover emotionally.'

기품.x: My grandmother has an air of grace, even at her age.
기품.e: Literally 'quality of spirit' — an elegance you sense from someone.

패기.ex: 그 신인 선수는 젊은 패기로 경기에 나섰어요.
패기.x: The rookie took to the field with youthful drive.

일사천리.m: swift progress without a hitch, in one smooth rush
일사천리.x: Everyone cooperated, so the work moved along swiftly without a hitch.
일사천리.e: Literally 'a river pouring a thousand miles in one rush'.
일사천리.t: Pronounced [일싸철리]; usually 일사천리로 진행되다 'to go quickly and smoothly'.

본말전도.m: putting the cart before the horse; getting priorities backward
본말전도.x: If you get hurt while exercising for your health, you've got things backward.
본말전도.e: Literally 'root and branch tip turned upside down.'

체계.ex: 이 회사는 교육 체계가 잘 갖춰져 있어요.
체계.x: This company has a well-organized training system.
체계.e: Literally 'body and lineage' — parts connected into a whole.
체계.t: 체계 is how parts are logically organized; 체제 is a political or institutional setup like 정치 체제.

시급성.ex: 정부는 이 문제의 시급성을 인식해야 합니다.
시급성.x: The government needs to recognize the urgency of this problem.

지속성.x: This medicine's effects last a long time.
지속성.t: For 'sustainability' in the environmental sense, Koreans usually say 지속 가능성.

시행규칙.ex: 신청 서류에 대한 자세한 내용은 시행규칙에 나와 있습니다.
시행규칙.x: Details about the application documents are given in the enforcement rules.
시행규칙.e: Ministry-level rules ranked below the decree: law, then 시행령, then 시행규칙.

임금체불.x: Many workers still suffer from unpaid wages.
임금체불.t: In casual speech, people say 월급이 밀렸어요 'my pay is overdue.'

투여.ex: 이 약은 하루에 두 번 투여해야 합니다.
투여.x: This drug must be administered twice a day.
투여.e: Literally 'throw in and give' — putting a drug into the body.
투여.t: 투여하다 is what medical staff do; the patient 복용하다 (takes) the medicine.

도체.x: Copper is a conductor that carries electricity well.
도체.e: Literally 'conducting body'. -체 = body, substance: 도체, 기체, 액체.

고수.ex: 고수는 북을 치며 소리꾼의 노래를 이끌어 줍니다.
고수.x: The drummer beats the drum and guides the singer's song.
고수.e: Literally 'drum hand'. Homonym alert: 고수 also means 'expert' and 'cilantro'.
고수.t: A famous saying, 일고수 이명창, ranks the drummer first and the singer second.

두루마기.ex: 할아버지는 설날에 한복 위에 두루마기를 입으셨어요.
두루마기.x: Grandpa wore a durumagi over his hanbok on Lunar New Year.
두루마기.e: Probably from 두루 (all around) + 막다 (block): a coat closed all around, without slits.

일갈하다.m: to shout (a rebuke), to roar out, to rebuke sharply
일갈하다.x: The teacher sharply rebuked the noisy students.
일갈하다.e: Literally 'one shout' — a single loud, sharp rebuke.

추산하다.x: Experts estimated the damage at about 10 billion won.

반론보도.ex: 그 회사는 기사에 대한 반론보도를 요구했습니다.
반론보도.x: The company demanded a right-of-reply report on the article.
반론보도.e: Literally 'counter-argument report': the subject of a story gets to tell their side.
반론보도.t: Pronounced [발론보도]: ㄴ becomes ㄹ next to ㄹ.

허비하다.m: to waste, to squander (time, money or energy)
허비하다.x: Don't waste your time on pointless things.
허비하다.e: Literally 'spend emptily' — using something up for nothing.

허겁지겁.m: hurriedly, in a frantic rush; greedily (eating)
허겁지겁.ex: 너무 배가 고파서 밥을 허겁지겁 먹었어요.
허겁지겁.x: I was so hungry that I wolfed down my food.
허겁지겁.t: Very often with eating: 허겁지겁 먹다 = to wolf down food.

다원주의.x: A democratic society is founded on pluralism.

소뇌.ex: 소뇌가 다치면 몸의 균형을 잡기 어렵습니다.
소뇌.x: If the cerebellum is injured, it's hard to keep your balance.
소뇌.e: Literally 'small brain', which is also what Latin 'cerebellum' means.
